title: Maternal exposure to cyclophosphamide during prepubertal life does not affect the cryosusceptibility of in vitro derived mouse embryos.
ehr_evidence: The study used healthy prepubertal female Swiss albino mice bred and housed in the Central Animal Research Facility of the Manipal Academy of Higher Education; no electronic health records were used.
summary: A controlled experimental mouse study evaluating whether prepubertal cyclophosphamide exposure (two weekly doses of 75 mg/kg at 2 weeks of age) affects cryosusceptibility and developmental competence of IVF-derived embryos.
key_findings: Significant decline in total ovarian follicle count in the CY group versus control (P<0.0001), with reduced primordial, preantral, and antral follicles (P<0.01–0.0001)
Fertilization rate comparable between control (84.3±6.8) and CY (88.3±4.9) groups
Post-warming embryo survival rate comparable between control (99.5±0.5) and CY (99±1) groups
No significant differences in blastocyst formation, apoptotic index, ICM outgrowth rate, or pluripotency marker (Oct4, Sox2, Nanog) expression between CY-exposed and control groups
Significant (P<0.01) downregulation of Oct4 and Sox2 transcript levels in CY in vitro-derived embryos versus in vivo-derived CY counterparts
captured_features: mRNA expression of Oct4, Sox2, and Nanog
study_design: controlled experimental animal study (mouse model) with treatment and control groups
population: prepubertal female Swiss albino mice exposed to cyclophosphamide at 2 weeks of age, assessed at reproductive phase
limitations: Mouse model limits direct human applicability
Single cyclophosphamide dosage tested, not clinical combination regimens
No in vivo implantation or post-implantation outcomes assessed
No direct dosage equivalence between mice and humans due to metabolic and pharmacokinetic differences
